content.title: About
content.content: Fruit waffles are a ready‑to‑eat frozen dessert consisting of crisp waffle layers filled with berry or fruit puree. The product is made from wheat flour, sugar, vegetable fats and natural fruit ingredients, then quickly frozen to preserve aroma and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Waffles first appeared in Europe in the 17th century as a way to use leftover batter.
Fruit fillings are often made from berries harvested in season and then frozen to retain vitamins.
Freezing allows the product to be stored for up to 12 months without flavor loss.
Fruit waffles are popular as a quick breakfast or snack in schools and offices.
IQF (Individually Quick Frozen) technology keeps pieces separate, preventing them from sticking together.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Waffles provide fast‑digesting carbs that give an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: The fruit layer is rich in vitamin C and other antioxidants that support the immune system.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many traditional desserts, these waffles usually contain less saturated fat.

items.title: Convenient and portable
items.content: They can be quickly heated in a microwave or toaster, making them practical for busy lifestyles.

items.title: Calcium and iron
items.content: Some recipes use fortified flour, increasing calcium and iron content.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Waffles are typically made with wheat flour, so they are not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fruit fillings may contain added sugar, which should be considered by individuals with diabetes or low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Over‑cooling
items.content: Improper reheating can make waffles too hard or overly soggy.

items.title: Freezer quality control
items.content: If stored above –18 °C, ice crystals can form, leading to texture and flavor degradation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen waffles in a microwave (30‑60 seconds) or toast them until golden. Serve with yogurt, honey, nuts or fresh berries for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the waffles in a sealed package at –18 °C or lower. After opening, use within 3‑4 weeks. Do not thaw and refreeze the product.
